context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Don't return every row from `UserModel.findAll()` on a route anyone can call. Put authentication middleware (for example `router.get('/users', requireAuth, handler)`) in front of every method on this route so a request with no valid session or token gets a 401. Inside the handler, decide what to return from the identity you verified (`req.user`), never from an id in the path, query or body. If the caller holds an authorised role (for example `req.user.role === 'admin'`, checked by `requireRole('admin')`), allow the full list, but use `UserModel.findAll({ attributes: ['id', 'name', 'email', 'role'] })` and add pagination with `limit` and `offset`, so password hashes, tokens and other fields that aren't needed stay out of the response. For any other caller, return only their own record with `UserModel.findOne({ where: { id: req.user.id }, attributes: [...] })`, or send a 403. On `/users/:id` style routes, apply the same check to GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE: allow the request only if `req.params.id === req.user.id` or the caller has an authorised role, and send a 403 otherwise. Log each access to Personal Data with the caller's id. Add tests showing that a request with no authentication gets a 401, a non-admin listing users gets a 403 or only their own record, and one user trying to read or change another user's id gets a 403. This meets the access control requirement in DPDP Rule 6(1)(b).
